expected_mechanism: LQR error model assumes small e_y, so a 0.081 rad bias (~4.6 deg) switches near the edge of LQR's linear range on a gentle curve; fault magnitude sits between R08-0055 (0.07 rad, failed) and R04-0030 (0.0795 rad, recovered) at same speed/friction.
Lower speed (20 vs 25 km/h) and lower friction (0.5) reduce lateral demand; 0.06 rad (~3.4 deg) bias sits near a boundary where higher friction or speed would push to failure.
Saturate at 0.8 on a mild curve exit; 0.3 s is between recovered (0.55 s, R04-0033) and failed (0.5 s, R10-0067) runs at same speed/friction, isolating duration as the boundary variable.
Higher friction (0.9) but negative side and shorter duration; boundary between R28048 recovered runs and R03-0028-... / R28048 saturated baseline.
Drift rate 0.014 rad/s sits between the only failed run (0.018 rad/s, R04-0032) and recovered baselines; slower drift gives LQR more time to correct before tracking divergence fires.
Faster drift at lower speed/friction; boundary probe toward the 0.018 rad/s failed run domain.

solver_fail at moderate speed (30 km/h) and medium friction (0.5) on a gentle curve entry; prior recovered run R09-0065 was at 25 km/h/0.6, so this probes the speed/friction boundary for LQR recovery after abrupt MPC loss.

intermittent_bias with 0.11 rad (~6.3 deg) on-time and 0.7 s off; boundary between the recovered run (0.09 rad, on=0.3, off=0.6) and the failed run (0.075 rad, on=0.5, off=0.7) at same speed/friction/route.
intermittent_bias with 0.085 rad and longer on-time; boundary toward the never-switched run at 0.0671 rad/on=0.89 and the recovered run at 0.0671 rad/on=0.81, isolating the on-time parameter.
